title: 01 — Create the Organization
html:
English |

01 — Create the Organization

The Organization is the first step of the journey — and it is what makes Golmet more than a loose validator: the company's products are born inside it, the shared knowledge lives in it, and the norms of how the team works accumulate in it. The full concept is in docs/concepts/organization.md; here is the step by step, on screen.

The wizard, screen by screen

the operator creates the company folder and runs:

mkdir MinhaOrganizacao && cd MinhaOrganizacao
golmet init

Since bare golmet init is always interactive (the kit never creates anything without asking), the wizard opens:

◆ What do you want to initialize? (↑/↓ move · enter confirms · esc cancels)

>   Organization the root that groups the workspaces
    Product workspace inside an existing Organization new project inside the root
    Free-root product workspace independent new project

An Organization is the company root that groups the workspaces. Create one if
you are structuring the company — the products are born inside it.

Notice: each option has a short description beside it, and the line below changes as the cursor moves — that is the active item's description, at the moment you need it. No jargon: the wizard says "Organization", not "container".

The operator moves to Organization and hits enter. The wizard asks for the name (empty = use the current folder). Then comes the Summary:

Summary:

  type:      Organization (container: true)
  root:      C:\company\MinhaOrganizacao
  files:     golmet.yaml · CONSTITUTION.md · INDEX.md

◆ Confirm and create? (ENTER confirms · n goes back to editing · esc cancels)

ENTER creates. (n goes back to the previous step — what you typed stays pre-filled; esc cancels everything without creating anything, at any step.)

What each created file keeps

The kit created three files — each one has a role in the journey:

  • golmet.yaml — the Organization's manifest. This is where the kit knows that this is an org (container: true), which versioning model is in effect (versioning: org-repo — the org is the repository and the products are folders of it) and which products exist (products: [], for now).
  • CONSTITUTION.md — the organization's principles: what is non-negotiable in the way of working. A stub to edit — it becomes a living document.
  • INDEX.md — the org's navigation: the index of products and documents.

And one more the kit created without announcing it: the .gitignore — because in an org-repo org the kit's work zone (.golmet/, where checkpoints and history live) is never versioned.

The step that is yours: versioning

The Organization was made to be your versioning repository — the products are born as folders inside it and version in its repo (the org-repo model). The kit creates the structure and the .gitignore; Git itself is your operation:

git init
git add -A
git commit -m "organization created — products to follow"

The already-created .gitignore protects the work zone .golmet/ from versioning (checkpoints and history never go up). From here, the org is a repo like any other — with the difference that every product folder you version inside it carries the whole workflow within.

The catalog

What the wizard didn't show: the Organization was just registered in the kit's global catalog, at ~/.golmet/organizations.json. Next time someone creates a product and picks "inside an existing Organization", the catalog's organizations show up in the list with their path beside them — no typing paths. The org's golmet.yaml is the source of truth; the catalog is just wizard convenience.

What comes next

An empty Organization does nothing on its own. The next step is being born inside it: 02 — create the project.
